result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternative actions or outcomes: Model an exclusive gateway before the alternative actions, with a separate outgoing branch for each alternative; do not model the alternatives as actions that all occur.

When the description states that the same process can be initiated through mutually exclusive alternative channels or methods: Model the alternatives with an exclusive gateway after the start event, with each outcome representing one alternative.

When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives for where or how an item is handled: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and separate alternative paths, then merge them before any shared next step.
When the description states that one outcome may be achieved through several distinct methods: Model the stated methods as explicit alternatives rather than subsuming them in one generic activity.
